item.title: Kerberoasting+PtH - DIY Lab
item.description:
Difficulty: Easy

OS: Windows

Date Completed: 2026-10-19

Write-up Authored by: Ian Simons

Lab Created by: Ian Simons

Core Competencies:

  • Active Directory Enumeration

  • LDAP Enumeration

  • Kerberos Authentication

  • Password Cracking

  • Pass the Hash

Overview

Recently I completed a Hack the Box lab called Active. This Box was a lot of fun and showed me that Active Directory is not some overly complex inherently hardened system. After that I decided that I wanted to learn more about attacking Active Directory on my own. I set up this lab to better understand and learn to run the Pass-the-Hash attack. There was a lot of learning involved, but I came away with a solid lab, and a much better understanding of the technique.

item.title: Active - Hack the Box
item.description:
Difficulty: Easy

OS: Windows

Date Completed: 2026-10-13

Write-up Authored by: Ian Simons

Challenge Created by: eks & mrb3n8132

Core Competencies:

  • Active Directory Enumeration

  • LDAP Enumeration

  • Kerberos Authentication

  • Password Cracking

Overview

This machine was discovered completely by accident. I had originally planned to complete a different box but accidentally scanned the wrong IP. After spending longer than I would care to admit attacking a web server I was convinced was an Active Directory Domain Controller, I decided to do Active instead. I am really glad I did. It helped break down the perceived complexity I had associated with Active Directory Machines, and demonstrated that successful domain compromise often results from methodical enumeration and chaining of realistic misconfigurations rather than highly complex exploitation techniques.

item.title: Write-up Generator with Nmap Integration
item.description:
Introduction

Recently I made a python tool to automate my write-up templates, start filling out some simple sections (ie nmap output, open ports etc), and perform a few additional Web Enumeration tasks such as grabbing html comments and the robots.txt file if it exists. I built it because I wanted to learn basic nmap output parsing, and save time during my weekly write-ups.This tool should save me time creating a skeleton of the write-up. It should also prevent accidentally leaving old data in new write-ups, and standardize my formatting for every write-up.
